title: Adaptive Cost Shield Controller for Region & Instance Routing
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We observe unpredictable spend spikes when traffic is routed aggressively to cheaper preemptible instances (cloud spot) across regions. Hard budget cutoffs create poor tail latency and request failures for latency-sensitive customers. We need a controller that lets routing prioritize cost while preserving SLOs via soft budget shields, graceful degradation to lower-fidelity model variants, and instance-type-aware admission.

Goal: Implement an adaptive 'Cost Shield' controller placed in the routing decision path that: (1) enforces per-customer soft budget caps (daily/hourly smoothing), (2) prefers preemptible/spot capacity when safe, (3) selects GPU instance classes by marginal latency/cost delta, and (4) degrades to cheaper model variants or smaller context sizes instead of hard-failing when budget pressure or evictions occur.
design_decisions: Controller sits between policy layer and cluster scheduler; no infra changes required for initial rollout (controller returns routing directives).
Soft budget model uses leaky-bucket smoothing (token bucket with decay) to avoid sharp cutoffs; thresholds map to routing profiles rather than binary allow/deny.
Instance selection uses a cost-latency delta matrix computed from recent telemetry aggregated by model, sequence-length percentile, and instance class.
Fallback chain: primary model variant -> quantized variant -> smaller model family -> queued with low-latency warning. Avoid returning HTTP 5xx for predictable budget throttles.
Eviction mitigation: preemptible-aware smoothing prefers instances with lower eviction probability for tail-sensitive customers and falls back regionally when eviction rate exceeds threshold.
Policy config must be per-tenant and support overrides (enterprise customers can set hard caps/hard preference for on-demand).
acceptance_criteria: Soft budget shields applied per-customer with smoothing window of 1h and 24h buckets configurable.
Mean request latency under shielded routing remains within 1.2x baseline for P95 for affected tenants.
Observed monthly cost reduction >= 12% for workloads routed with Cost Shield under typical traffic patterns (benchmarked in staging).
Automated fallback to cheaper model variant triggered on budget threshold without client-visible error; logs contain explanation and route_reason.
Integration tests that simulate spot eviction storms show <0.5% request failures due to budget enforcement, and fallback paths exercised.
implementation_steps: 1) Build Cost Shield microservice: REST endpoint that returns routing hints (region, instance_class, model_variant, priority_tier) and advisory 'reason' tags.
2) Telemetry: extend metrics pipeline to emit per-instance eviction probability and cost-latency deltas; add aggregation jobs for 1h/24h tokens.
3) Admission logic: modify routing outbox to accept hints and apply them via current scheduler adapter (no direct scheduler patch required).
4) Fallback mechanics: implement variant selector with ordered list and score thresholds; compute graceful downgrade steps for the call path.
5) UI/Console: surface active shield state and per-tenant budget burn-down in Console Cost > Routing tab.
6) Rollout: feature-gated rollout starting with internal alpha tenants, staged to canary customers, then opt-in beta before defaulting on non-enterprise accounts.
monitoring_and_alerts: Metric: shield_activation_rate per-tenant; alert if >10% sustained for 6 hours (possible misconfiguration).
Metric: fallback_rate_to_lower_variant; alert if >5% with customer_impact=high label.
Metric: spot_eviction_rate_by_region; automated re-routing if eviction_rate > 0.08 for 15m.
Cost metric: effective_cost_per_token routed_with_shield (compare to baseline).
SLOs: P95 latency and error rate for shielded requests instrumented and tracked in dashboard 'Cost Shield - Health'.
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket smoothing and decision thresholds.
Integration tests: simulate bursty traffic and ensure smoothing avoids hard clamp and triggers downgrades only when thresholds met.
Chaos tests: induce simulated spot evictions in staging clusters and verify automatic regional fallback and variant downgrades.
Load tests: validate routing hints do not add >3ms median request overhead at 20k rps.
E2E: deploy to canary tenant and run A/B comparison of cost, latency, and customer-visible degradations for 2 weeks.
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal) - 2 days: validate metrics and rollback behavior.
Canary - 2 weeks: 3 low-risk external tenants, continuous monitoring and daily check-ins.
Beta - 4 weeks: opt-in for non-enterprise customers via Console toggle.
GA: enable by default for all non-enterprise tenants with opt-out within console.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect thresholds throttle healthy customers -> Mitigation: default to conservative thresholds and require tenant opt-in for aggressive savings.
Risk: Decision latency added by controller -> Mitigation: cache routing hints for 10s for similar request signatures and fall back to safe default when controller unavailable.
Risk: Complexity in billing reconciliation when model variant changes mid-request -> Mitigation: bill by actual executed tokens; annotate billing records with routing_hint_id for audits.
Risk: Enterprise customers require hard guarantees -> Mitigation: provide hard-cap mode that disables downgrade and returns explicit error/notify instead.

notes: Do not hardcode model names in controller; use model_id and variant tags to keep routing generic.
We will maintain an audit log of routing decisions for at least 90 days for enterprise compliance requests.
